notes: Account summary: large fintech payments platform evaluating dedicated GPU pools across multiple regions for low-latency fraud-scoring and chat ops.
Primary ask: reserved GPU planning with explicit failover headroom and contractual throughput guarantees rather than best-effort capacity.
Business drivers: reduce fraud detection variance during peak payroll cycles; keep interactive chat latency <200ms p95 for ops users; maintain predictable unit cost under reserved commit.

Key metrics they want in contract: availability SLA (99.9%), p99 latency targets for short completions (<=400ms), sustained throughput guarantee of 2k req/s for embeddings/rerank (mixed sizes), and explicit failover RTO (90s preferred) when a region/AZ degrades.

Capacity strategy discussed: 3 primary GPU pools (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with 25% warm-headroom per pool for failover, cross-region capacity reservations to be billed differently from burst, hot-standby vs cold-standby tradeoffs covered.
Ask from Infra: detailed model footprint matrix (seq len profiles, kv-cache sizes, memory/VRAM per model variant) to finalize GPU counts; provided initial CSV of top-10 prompt patterns.

Operational requirements: monthly DR runbooks, canary rollouts for model changes, automated traffic routing with policy-based failover (latency-first, cost-fallback), and traceable audit logs for token-level access.
Security notes: must support customer-managed KMS, contract clause for EU data residency, SOC2 evidence pack requested during procurement window.
Quote from CTO (paraphrase): 'We cannot accept opaque failover — need defined cold/warm headroom and a playbook for cross-region evacuation.',

Negotiation points flagged: how surge/burst is priced against reserved capacity, SLA credits calculation method (per-region vs global), scheduled maintenance windows and notice periods, and minimum lead time for capacity scale-ups.

POC plan: 4-week pilot that validates latency SLOs under synthetic peak traffic, failover time-tests between us-east and eu-west, and cost delta analysis for reserved vs burst usage. Pilot to run with two model variants (full FP16 and 4-bit quantized) to compare perf/cost.
Decision criteria: meets p99 and throughput SLOs during simulated peak, legal accepts SLA, and cost per 1M tokens <= internal target (TBD).

Internal Redwood asks: confirm ability to reserve exact GPU counts per AZ, show historical node-failure impacts, provide draft SLA language and failure credit calc, and list standard maintenance blackout windows.
Next AE tasks: send SOW v1.2, attach model footprint CSV, and schedule legal + infra sync for 2026-03-18.
Status: technical evaluation progressing; procurement/legal review gating contract signature.
